body.hook: In Alberta, you can start an apprenticeship while still in high school, earn a wage, and get credit for both school and your trade. The Registered Apprenticeship Program (RAP) is one of the best-kept secrets in high school.

study.title: Ready for Work
study.question: What skills and programs help high school students get into the workplace?
study.passage:
Part 1, Employability skills (10 minutes): Sort these into three groups: fundamental (communicate, manage information, think and solve problems), personal management (be positive, responsible, adaptable, learn continuously, work safely) and teamwork (work with others, participate in projects). These come from the Conference Board of Canada's Employability Skills.
Part 2, Workplace learning options in Alberta (15 minutes):
• Registered Apprenticeship Program (RAP): start a trade apprenticeship as a high school student; hours count toward your apprenticeship and earn high school credits; you are paid.
• Work Experience 15, 25, 35: supervised, unpaid or paid work placements for credit.
• Green Certificate: agricultural apprenticeship-style training for credit.
• Dual credit: courses that count for both high school and post-secondary.
Part 3, Skills evidence (10 minutes): For five employability skills, write evidence from school, sports, volunteering or CTS ("Teamwork: led my group's café service for 40 customers").
Part 4, Résumé (20 minutes): Draft a one-page résumé: contact, profile (two lines), skills with evidence, education, experience and volunteering, references available on request.
study.source: Original career task written for this lesson; program details summarized from Alberta Education and Conference Board of Canada sources.
